q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a foam mattress?
title: Foam mattress carbon footprint
short: Work out the foam weight from density and volume, multiply by the foam's footprint from the supplier or a published dataset, and add springs, fabric, adhesives, the plant's energy per mattress and the packaging. Polyol and isocyanate in the foam usually make up the largest share.
audience: Mattress and foam makers supplying retailers, hotels and e-commerce

p: Foam weight = density x volume. A queen mattress of 1.5 m x 1.9 m with 0.15 m of foam has 0.4275 cubic metres; at 32 kg per cubic metre that is 13.7 kg of foam. Do this for each foam layer, since memory foam, HR foam and rebonded foam have different densities.

ul: Pocketed or bonnell springs: steel wire by weight.
Quilting fabric, fibre fill and border tape.
Plant energy: foaming, cutting, quilting, bonding and compressing.

p: India phased out HCFC-141b in foam manufacturing from 1 January 2020 under its HCFC Phase-out Management Plan. Most slabstock foam is now water-blown, where the reaction of water with isocyanate forms CO2. If you use any other blowing agent, record the quantity and its global warming potential, because releases count in Scope 1.

Many mattress makers buy blocks from a foamer and only cut, bond and cover. Then the foam is a bought-in input: ask the foamer for kg CO2e per kg of each grade and keep your own plant energy separate.

example.title: Worked example: plant electricity per mattress (one month)
lines: Plant electricity: 14,200 / 2,500 = 5.68 kg CO2 per mattress
Foam: 13.7 kg per queen mattress x the foamer's factor per kg gives the larger part
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
